tool: Codex CLI built-in image generation through the imggen skill; transparent requests for the prop sheets
battlefield_prompt_template:
Painted fantasy battlefield background for a turn-based hex strategy game. Wide 16:9 landscape image, seen from a high three-quarter top-down angle (about 55 degrees down), in the tradition of classic 1990s fantasy strategy battle screens, but painted with modern detail. Match the camera angle, the layout, the lighting softness and the painterly rendering of the {REFROLE}.

Composition:
- The central 75% of the image is one open, flat, calm {FIELD}. Keep it low in contrast and evenly lit so that small painted figures and a thin hex grid stay readable on top of it. No {FORBIDDEN} or objects anywhere in this central field.
- Along the top edge, a narrow band (about the top 14% of the image) showing {TOP}, seen at a slight angle and fading into light haze.
- On the far left and far right edges (outer 12% on each side), {SIDES}, where an army commander could stand.
- The bottom edge darkens a little with {BOTTOM} in the near foreground.

Light: {LIGHT}

Style: painterly digital illustration with visible fine brush texture, rich but natural colours{PALETTE}.

No people, no animals, no creatures, no buildings, no text, no UI, no hex grid lines, no border.
prop_prompt_template:
A sheet of five separate hand-painted obstacle props for the battlefield of a turn-based fantasy hex strategy game, on a genuinely transparent background. Every prop stands alone with wide empty transparent space around it; nothing touches or overlaps, and nothing is cut off by the image edge. All props are seen from the same high three-quarter top-down angle (about 55 degrees down) as the battlefield in the reference image, lit softly from the upper left, in a painterly style with visible fine brush texture and rich natural colours that match that {FAMILY} battlefield. Do not paint the battlefield itself.

Top row, three compact props, each sized to fill one hexagonal tile and about as wide as it is deep: {S1}; {S2}; {S3}.
Bottom row, two wide props, each about twice as wide as it is deep, sized to stretch across two hexagonal tiles side by side: {D1}; {D2}.

Each prop sits on a small, irregular tuft of its own ground ({BASE}) that fades out at its rim. No ground plane between the props, no cast shadows on the background, no frame, no labels, no text, no people and no creatures.
notes: The grass battlefield is the painted meadow of the signed-off battle mockup (2026-10-09). Every other battlefield takes its camera, layout and rendering from it and its palette from the family's earlier ground texture; each prop sheet takes its colours and light from its family's battlefield. Masters stay out of Git; tools/build_battlefield_art.py derives the runtime art from them.

Every prop stands alone with wide empty transparent space around it; nothing touches or overlaps, and nothing is cut off by the image edge. All props are seen from the same high three-quarter top-down angle (about 55 degrees down) as the battlefield in the reference image, lit softly from the upper left, in a painterly style with visible fine brush texture and rich natural colours that match that rough badlands battlefield. Do not paint the battlefield itself.

Top row, three compact props, each sized to fill one hexagonal tile and about as wide as it is deep: a rounded red sandstone boulder; a pile of broken sandstone slabs; a weathered red rock spire.
Bottom row, two wide props, each about twice as wide as it is deep, sized to stretch across two hexagonal tiles side by side: a low layered sandstone ledge; two eroded red boulders side by side.

Each prop sits on a small, irregular tuft of its own ground (dry reddish earth, gravel and dry grass) that fades out at its rim. No ground plane between the props, no cast shadows on the background, no frame, no labels, no text, no people and no creatures.

1: a rounded red sandstone boulder
a pile of broken sandstone slabs
a weathered red rock spire
2: a low layered sandstone ledge
two eroded red boulders side by side
